arguments.sql_query: WITH ibd_patients AS (SELECT DISTINCT co.person_id FROM omop.condition_occurrence co JOIN omop.concept_ancestor ca ON ca.descendant_concept_id = co.condition_concept_id WHERE ca.ancestor_concept_id IN (4074815,201606,81893)), categories AS (SELECT 'Arthritis (broad)' AS comorbidity, 4291025 AS ancestor_concept_id UNION ALL SELECT 'Inflammatory polyarthropathy', 74125 UNION ALL SELECT 'Spondyloarthritis', 37205058 UNION ALL SELECT 'Axial spondyloarthritis', 36716891 UNION ALL SELECT 'Ankylosing spondylitis', 437082 UNION ALL SELECT 'Psoriatic arthritis', 40319772 UNION ALL SELECT 'Psoriasis', 140168 UNION ALL SELECT 'Uveitis', 4028363 UNION ALL SELECT 'Anterior uveitis', 4132792 UNION ALL SELECT 'Iritis', 4274964 UNION ALL SELECT 'Episcleritis', 4218083 UNION ALL SELECT 'Erythema nodosum', 140176 UNION ALL SELECT 'Pyoderma gangrenosum', 133283 UNION ALL SELECT 'Primary sclerosing cholangitis', 4058821 UNION ALL SELECT 'Venous thrombosis', 444247 UNION ALL SELECT 'Deep venous thrombosis', 4133004 UNION ALL SELECT 'Pulmonary embolism', 440417), hits AS (SELECT c.comorbidity, co.person_id FROM categories c JOIN omop.concept_ancestor ca ON ca.ancestor_concept_id = c.ancestor_concept_id JOIN omop.condition_occurrence co ON co.condition_concept_id = ca.descendant_concept_id JOIN ibd_patients ip ON ip.person_id = co.person_id) SELECT comorbidity, COUNT(DISTINCT person_id) AS n_patients, CAST(100.0 * COUNT(DISTINCT person_id) / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ibd_patients) AS DECIMAL(6,2)) AS pct_of_ibd FROM hits GROUP BY comorbidity ORDER BY n_patients DESC

In this OMOP EHR IBD cohort (`n=27,774`), the most frequent extraintestinal comorbidities I found were:

| Comorbidity | IBD patients | % of IBD cohort |
|---|---:|---:|
| Arthritis, broad | 5,922 | 21.32% |
| Venous thrombosis | 1,844 | 6.64% |
| Deep venous thrombosis | 1,110 | 4.00% |
| Psoriasis | 1,010 | 3.64% |
| Spondyloarthritis | 915 | 3.29% |
| Inflammatory polyarthropathy | 904 | 3.25% |
| Pulmonary embolism | 693 | 2.50% |
| Primary sclerosing cholangitis | 469 | 1.69% |
| Uveitis | 441 | 1.59% |
| Axial spondyloarthritis | 418 | 1.51% |
| Ankylosing spondylitis | 411 | 1.48% |
| Pyoderma gangrenosum | 225 | 0.81% |
| Erythema nodosum | 202 | 0.73% |

Interpretation: the dominant extraintestinal signal is musculoskeletal inflammation, especially broad arthritis/spondyloarthritis. A plausible shared mechanism is gut–joint immune crosstalk driven by Th17/IL-23 signaling, TNF-α, IL-6, and innate myeloid activation. Barrier dysfunction and microbial antigen exposure in IBD can prime mucosal T cells that traffic to joints, skin, and eye via shared adhesion/chemokine programs.

Other patterns fit related immune axes:

- **Psoriasis / psoriatic arthritis**: IL-23–Th17–IL-17 pathway overlap with Crohn’s/UC biology.
- **Uveitis / iritis / episcleritis**: systemic Th1/Th17 inflammation and HLA-associated mucosal–ocular immune activation.
- **Pyoderma gangrenosum / erythema nodosum**: neutrophilic and panniculitic inflammation, often tracking systemic inflammatory burden.
- **Primary sclerosing cholangitis**: gut–liver axis, aberrant lymphocyte homing, bile duct immune injury; strongly linked to UC.
- **Venous thrombosis / PE/DVT**: inflammation-induced hypercoagulability via cytokine-driven endothelial activation, platelet activation, tissue factor, and impaired fibrinolysis.

Caveat: these are EHR diagnosis-code frequencies, not adjudicated prevalence; broad concepts like “arthritis” may include nonspecific or degenerative disease, so the more specific spondyloarthritis/uveitis/PSC/skin diagnoses are more biologically interpretable.
